title: Infinite Sequence Generator with Step
problemStatement: Implement a generator function `stepSequence(start, step, max)` that yields numbers starting at `start`, incrementing by `step`, until reaching or exceeding `max`.
interviewTrap: Forgetting that generators are lazy; calling `stepSequence()` does not execute code until `.next()` is called.

testCases.name: Generates correct sequence from 0 to 6 with step 2

details.name: Generates correct sequence from 0 to 6 with step 2

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Generator functions (`function*`) implement the Iterable and Iterator protocols (ECMA-262 §27.1). Unlike standard functions that run to completion, generators can pause execution via `yield` and resume when `.next()` is called, enabling lazy evaluation of infinite sequences without memory exhaustion.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Execute `yield current` to pause execution and emit `{ value: current, done: false }`.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: When a generator function is invoked, V8 does not execute its body immediately; instead, it returns an exotic GeneratorObject containing a heap-allocated Execution Context snapshot. When `.next()` is called, V8 restores the execution context onto the call stack, evaluates until the next `yield` bytecode, suspends the context, and returns the yielded value.

complexity.space: O(1) heap memory for the generator state object (does not allocate sequence elements in memory).

edgeCasesHandled: Zero step or negative step increments.
Infinite progression without memory leaks or call stack overflow.
Generates clean standard `{ value, done }` iteration protocol objects.

specifications: ECMA-262 §27.5 GeneratorFunction Objects and Iterator Protocol
V8 Dev Blog: Generator Suspension and Resume bytecodes (SuspendGenerator, ResumeGenerator)
verifiedRules: Generators pause at yield points without consuming CPU cycles.
Next invocation resumes from exact program counter and lexical scope position.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is the difference between a Generator Function and a Generator Object?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: A Generator Function (`function*`) is the constructor definition. When invoked, it does NOT execute its body; instead, it returns a Generator Object. The Generator Object conforms to both the Iterable protocol (`[Symbol.iterator]()`) and the Iterator protocol (`.next()`, `.return()`, `.throw()`). Execution only begins when `.next()` is called.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of generator instantiation vs execution.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does the 'yield*' operator differ from standard 'yield'?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `yield` emits a single value and pauses. `yield*` delegates iteration to another iterable or generator: it iterates through the target iterable, yielding each of its values sequentially, and evaluates to the return value of the delegated generator.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests knowledge of generator composition and recursion.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Can an infinite generator cause a memory leak?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: No! Unlike an infinite array (which would exhaust memory), an infinite generator evaluates lazily on demand. It stores only its current execution context on the heap and consumes O(1) memory, advancing only when `.next()` is explicitly called by a consumer.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Checks understanding of lazy evaluation vs eager memory allocation.

realWorldUseCases.description: Generating incremental or algorithmic sequence numbers lazily without holding pre-allocated IDs in memory.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: function* idGen() { let id = 1; while (true) yield id++; }

realWorldUseCases.description: Abstracting paginated API endpoints so consumers can loop using `for...of` without knowing about page boundaries.

howToExplain.opening: Generators are functions that can be paused and resumed on demand, implementing the Iterable and Iterator protocols to enable memory-efficient lazy evaluation.
keyPoints: Invoking a generator function returns an exotic GeneratorObject without executing code.
yield pauses execution and returns { value, done: false }.
Calling .next() resumes execution from the exact point of suspension.
Generators allow representing infinite data streams in O(1) memory.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Generators bring coroutine semantics to JavaScript, laying the architectural foundation for async/await and streaming iterators.
analogies: A DVD player: you press 'Play' (next), watch until a chapter marker, press 'Pause' (yield), and come back later to resume from the exact same frame.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using for...of on a generator without a termination condition, expecting it to stop.
commonMistakes.why: A for...of loop on an infinite generator will loop forever and freeze the thread.
commonMistakes.correct: Always break out of infinite generator loops using a break statement or limit condition.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does V8 implement generator suspension and resumption in bytecode?
followUpDeepDive.answer: V8's Ignition interpreter uses dedicated bytecodes: `SuspendGenerator` snapshots local registers into the heap-allocated GeneratorObject. When `.next()` is called, `ResumeGenerator` restores registers onto the Call Stack and jumps directly to the saved bytecode offset.
